## Claims
- [proved] Let \(i,j\ge1\), \(0\le b\le\min(i,j)\), \(a\ge0\), and \(\rho\subseteq b^a\). Then
\[
 \sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|}
 \omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})s_{(i^j,\sigma)}
 =(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}.
\]
- [source-backed] The indicated lower-adjoined Schur classes generate \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 228-235]

## Strategy
Put \(h_m=0\) for \(m<0\), \(h_0=1\), and \(N=j+a+b\).  Write
\[
U_l=j+l-b\quad(1\le l\le a+b).
\]
Define the ordered \(N\times N\) bordered matrix \(M_\rho\), with rows
\[
T_1,\ldots,T_j,U_1,\ldots,U_{a+b}
\]
and columns
\[
Q_1,\ldots,Q_{j+a},D_1,\ldots,D_b,
\]
by
\[
M_\rho(T_p,Q_q)=h_{i-p+q},\qquad M_\rho(T_p,D_c)=0,
\]
\[
M_\rho(U_l,Q_q)=h_{q-U_l},\qquad
M_\rho(U_l,D_c)=h_{\rho'_c+b+1-c-l}.
\tag{1}
\]

For \(\sigma=(\sigma _1,\ldots,\sigma_a)\subseteq b^a\), set
\[
S_\sigma=\{l_p=b+p-\sigma_p:1\le p\le a\},
\quad
R_\sigma=\{1,\ldots,j\}\cup\{j+l:l\in S_\sigma\},
\quad
C_\sigma=\{1,\ldots,j+a\}.
\]
The \(l_p\) are strictly increasing, so \(\sigma\mapsto S_\sigma\) bijects partitions in \(b^a\) with \(a\)-subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,a+b\}\). Thus every Laplace term along the first \(j+a\) columns is indexed by exactly one \(\sigma\subseteq b^a\). Its complementary sets are
\[
R_\sigma^c=\{j+l:l\notin S_\sigma\},\qquad
C_\sigma^c=\{j+a+1,\ldots,j+a+b\}.
\]

The principal minor is Jacobi–Trudi:
\[
\det M_\rho[R_\sigma,C_\sigma]
=\det\!\bigl(h_{(i^j,\sigma)_r-r+q}\bigr)_{1\le r,q\le j+a}
=s_{(i^j,\sigma)}.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(K_\sigma=\{k_1<\cdots<k_b\}=\{1,\ldots,a+b\}\setminus S_\sigma\), then
\[
k_t=t+\sigma'_{b+1-t}.
\tag{3}
\]
Reversing the \(b\) complementary rows and transposing gives
\[
\det M_\rho[R_\sigma^c,C_\sigma^c]
=(-1)^{\binom b2}
\det\!\bigl(h_{\rho'_c-\sigma'_r-c+r}\bigr)_{r,c=1}^b
=(-1)^{\binom b2}s_{\rho'/\sigma'}.
\tag{4}
\]
This is zero precisely when \(\sigma\nsubseteq\rho\); for \(\sigma\subseteq\rho\), it is the nonzero skew Schur function. Hence exactly the requested minors survive.

The Laplace sign is
\[
\sum R_\sigma
=\frac{j(j+1)}2+aj+ab+\frac{a(a+1)}2-|\sigma|,
\]
\[
\sum C_\sigma=\frac{(j+a)(j+a+1)}2.
\]
Set
\[
F=\frac{j(j+1)}2+aj+ab+\frac{a(a+1)}2+
\frac{(j+a)(j+a+1)}2.
\]
Laplace expansion, (2), and (4) yield
\[
\det M_\rho
=(-1)^{F+\binom b2}
\sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}(-1)^{|\sigma|}
s_{\rho'/\sigma'}s_{(i^j,\sigma)}.
\tag{5}
\]

For completeness, the fixed-border Jacobi–Trudi reduction is
\[
\det M_\rho
=(-1)^{F+\binom b2}
s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}.
\tag{6}
\]
Indeed, successively expand the \(D_b,D_{b-1},\ldots,D_1\) border against the \(U\)-rows. The relation \(k_t=t+\sigma'_{b+1-t}\) identifies the surviving row shifts with
\[
i+\rho'_1-1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b-b,\ i-(b+1),\ldots,i-j,
\]
in reverse order for the first \(b\) shifts. Reordering these rows contributes
\((-1)^{\binom b2}\); moving the \(a+b\) border rows past the first \(j\) rows and the first \(j+a\) columns contributes \((-1)^F\). The resulting \(j\times j\) determinant is
\[
\det\bigl(h_{i+\rho'_r-r+c}\bigr)_{\substack{1\le r\le b\\1\le c\le j}}
\ \text{with rows }\
\det\bigl(h_{i-r+c}\bigr)_{\substack{b<r\le j\\1\le c\le j}},
\]
namely the Jacobi–Trudi determinant on the right side of (6).

Combining (5) and (6), using \(\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})=s_{\rho'/\sigma'}\), gives the claimed identity after multiplication by \((-1)^{|\rho|}\).

Boundary cases: if \(\rho=\varnothing\), only \(\sigma=\varnothing\) occurs and the formula is \(s_{i^j}=s_{i^j}\). If \(a=0\), necessarily \(\rho=\sigma=\varnothing\), with the same conclusion. If \(b=j\), the terminal block \(i^{j-b}\) is empty; all determinants above remain valid. Empty determinants are \(1\).

Projecting only now to \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) preserves the identity. Since the classes \(s_{(i^j,\sigma)}\) lie in \(J_v\), its image in \(J_v/A_+J_v\) has all proper-\(\sigma\) terms zero, because
\[
\deg s_{\rho'/\sigma'}=|\rho|-|\sigma|>0.
\]
Thus
\[
[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]
=(-1)^{|\rho|}
[\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}].
\]
